description: Abbott Laboratories is a global health care company. Founded in 1888, the company operates in four main segments: established pharmaceutical products, diagnostic products, nutritional products—including infant formula—and medical devices. As of 2024, Abbott’s medical devices segment was its largest and fastest-growing, accounting for about 45% of revenue. That segment includes devices for monitoring cardiovascular health, glucose monitoring systems for diabetes care, and neuromodulation devices for chronic pain and movement disorders.

rankings.title: Change the World
rankings.itemDescription: The transfusion division of health care giant Abbott screens about half of the U.S. blood supply, so the nationwide decline in blood donations since the COVID pandemic has been not only a public health problem but, for Abbott, a business problem. The company tackled the dilemma by appealing to college students’ competitive streak: Last year, it launched the “We Give Blood” campaign among students at schools in the Big Ten conference, coinciding with the college football season. The 2024 initiative resulted in nearly 20,000 donations, enough to save up to 60,000 lives. First-time donors represented 69% of We Give Blood participants. In and around the University of Nebraska—the school that won the competition—local blood centers saw a 27% increase in young donors (ages 16 to 24) versus the previous year. Season two kicked off this September, and is attracting donors at an even faster rate: It neared 20,000 donations in just the first four weeks of the drive.

rankings.title: Change the World
rankings.itemDescription:
Student debt is a massive burden in the U.S. There are more than 43 million borrowers carrying a combined $1.8 trillion in obligations. Debtors often have to choose between paying off their student loans or saving for retirement. That’s why Abbott developed Freedom 2 Save. F2S is a benefit program in which enrolled employees who put 2% of their pay toward their student loans get a corporate match of 5% into their 401(k)s—keeping them from having to sacrifice their future to pay off their past. The health care company’s innovative offering required special permission from the IRS before it could launch in 2018. To date, Abbott has contributed more than $5.5 million to over 2,500 of its employees, including $1.7 million in 2022 alone.

Beginning in 2024, all U.S. employers will be able to offer a similar benefit through a provision of the SECURE 2.0 Act—inspired by Abbott’s offering—which will enable employers to match employees’ student loan payments with 401(k) contributions.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription:
Riding the tail end of a sales boom in COVID-19 tests, the medical device and health care products firm dropped 13 spots on the Fortune 500 in 2022, with revenue increasing only 1.3% and profits down 2%.

  • COVID-19 test revenue accounted for one-fifth of Abbott’s bottom line in 2022, jumping to $8.4 billion from $7.7 billion in 2021. At the end of the first quarter of 2023, the firm projected test sales to drop to $1.5 billion for the year.

  • Abbott fed some of its COVID-19 test proceeds into research and development, investing an additional $2 billion in 2022.

  • The Department of Justice is investigating Abbott’s infant formula plant in Michigan, which shut down from February to June 2022 owing to contamination, setting off a nationwide shortage.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: COVID-19 testing continued to drive revenue growth for Abbott Labs in 2021: As of January 2022, the company had distributed about 1.4 billion tests, and those generated $7.7 billion in sales in 2021. Medical devices and nutrition products like Similac and Ensure together account for about two-thirds of Abbott’s revenue. The nutrition division endured a setback in early 2022, however, when Abbott issued a voluntary recall of powdered infant formula manufactured in one of its facilities in Michigan after the plant was linked to a bacterial-infection outbreak; the shutdown contributed to a nationwide formula shortage.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: Abbott Laboratories leveled up on this year’s Global 500 list, leaping from last year’s rank of 393 to No. 350. Why? COVID testing. Abbott was one of the first to jump into the testing market, and that alacrity has paid off; the company’s diagnostics unit, which also houses its COVID test arm, raked in more than $4 billion in sales during the first quarter of 2021 alone. Abbott, though, isn’t putting all its eggs in one basket. As life starts returning to normal, the company believes its diabetes care and glucose monitoring products will continue to fuel growth.

rankings.title: Change the World
rankings.itemDescription:
Health care access is a challenge in Rwanda, which makes one diagnostic innovation by Abbott Labs particularly valuable. Abbott’s prenatal panel tests simultaneously for syphilis, malaria, HIV, and hepatitis B, using only one finger-stick of blood, with results in the same visit. For expectant mothers who may have time or resources for only one trip to the clinic, that means better care; the test has also enabled a tripling of malaria case detections.

At press time, health care providers were just beginning to deploy another potentially crucial Abbott diagnostic product: An “antigen” test for COVID-19 that yields results in 15 minutes and costs $5.
